segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: OK, welcome back to the new term. Hope you've had a good break and that you're looking forward to writing your dissertation . . . What I'd like to do in this session is give you the opportunity to ask questions on writing the dissertation . . . requirements, milestones . . . who to see when you need help. It's very informal... it may all be written on paper, but it's nice to get it confirmed. So anything you'd like to ask?

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: Dr Simon, is there a fixed hand-in date yet?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: Right. I can confirm that that's 21 May, not 20 as we first stated. OK? . . . Jane?

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: What about the word limit?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: Well we try to be pretty flexible on this, but in broad terms it's 18-20,000.

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: A h . . .

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: And you can choose your topics . . . anything from Years 2 and 3 . . . Yes?

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: I still haven't got any idea what I want to do it on. Who .. . ?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: Well, you should see your course tutor to agree on your final title and you should also be aware that there's a special programme running on research methods for anyone who wants some extra help on that.

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: Can I just check on the deadlines for everything?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: Yes, sure. Look, let me write it on the board . . . when the different stages have to be completed. First of all you've got to work on your basic bibliography, and that's due in to your course tutor by 31 January . . . which is just two weeks away, so you'd better get a move on on that.

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: Do we have to have our own draft plan by then?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: No, your draft plan is due on 7 February, which is a week later, so that . should give you plenty of time.

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: And when do we have to be doing the research?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: That's over a one-month period . . . essentially February to March.

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: And the write up?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: Well, you can't really get going on your writing until you've got quite a bit of the research done, so that's really March to May, with the hand in date on 21st. Any more questions?

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: Well, sir, just some advice really. It's about computers . .. would you advise us to buy one?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: What can 1 say, Andy? I know it's a massive expense, but I really feel that it will be of great benefit... you can always look in the Student Union adverts for second hand ones. Yes?

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: I've been looking at some of last year's dissertations.

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: Is that a good idea, sir? I heard . . .

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: Well, I don't think you should read them in detail too early or you might end up taking more of their ideas than you realise. But yes . . . it really is the best guide you can have to the expectations of the . . . of what's expected when you write a dissertation.

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: Sorry, Jane, I interrupted you.

segments.speaker: JANE
segments.en: That's OK. It's just that they did a lot of research using questionnaires . . . is that a good idea?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: I think questionnaires are very good at telling you how people questionnaires, but to be frank they tell you very little else. Avoid them!

segments.speaker: ANDY
segments.en: About interviews . . . is it OK if we interview you?

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: The tutors? I don't see why not; they don't have any special contribution to make, but you can if you want. There's a whole section on this issue in the Research Guide. I'm afraid it's slightly out of date, and you're probably better talking to the tutor on the Research Methods course, but you might find it useful to start there. ANDY/JANE OK, thanks.

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: OK . . . well, great, I hope that sorted a few things out. You can always come and see me or drop me a note if you've got any more queries. ANDY/JANE Fine.

segments.speaker: DR SIMON
segments.en: OK. Thanks . . .
